title: Skillonomia external pilot record
description: The record `node ci/run-pilot.mjs run` writes and `node ci/run-pilot.mjs verify` reads. It carries what a reviewer needs to re-check a pilot from outside it: the platform and the official path, the artifact identity its registry can be asked about, the candidate SHA, the URL the owner reads the receipt back from, the /health hash, the timestamps, the terminal receipt and its read-back hash, the transcript hash, the time to the first `adopted` and the blockers the run reproduced. It carries no credential, no API key, no user name and no machine path: the read-back credential travels in a token file named on the command line, which is its only copy. `additionalProperties` is false everywhere, so a field nobody designed cannot arrive carrying one.

outcome.description: `adopted` is a run that reached a terminal receipt; `blocked` is one that reproduced a blocker and stopped. A blocked run still writes a record, and its exit code is not zero.

rehearsal.description: True when the owner's verification URL is the runner's own loopback, so no external read-back was exercised. A rehearsal record never produces PILOTS_OK.

path.description: The one official path this pilot used. §C gives each pilot a choice of one, not both.

checksum.description: The npm registry's own integrity string for the tarball that was installed, or null on the container path.

digest.description: The immutable image digest that was pulled, or null on the npm path.

candidate_sha.description: The exact source commit the artifact was built from. Both pilot records name the same one.

verification_base_url.description: Where the owner reaches this deployment for a read-only receipt read-back until acceptance.

read_back_hash.description: The hash of the receipt as the server read it back, over its keys in sorted order. The verifier re-reads the receipt and recomputes this.

transcript.description: The redacted runner transcript, named by file name and read from beside the record — a path would name somebody's machine.

time_to_first_adopted_ms.description: From the first line of the run to the terminal receipt, in milliseconds. Null on a blocked run.

blockers.description: Only what the run itself reproduced: each entry names the probe that was re-executed and how many times it answered the same way. There is no option for adding one by hand.

record_hash.description: A checksum over this record's other fields, keys in sorted order. It detects an edit that did not recompute it; it is not a signature, and the checks that catch a recomputed edit are the transcript hash, the artifact read-back and the live receipt.
